Paris

Best Things To Do In Paris With Kids

By Priya Anand · April 25, 2026 · Updated August 21, 2026 · 8 min read

Paris has a reputation as a sophisticated, adult-paced city, which can make it feel like an odd choice for a family trip. In practice, it works very well with kids — as long as the itinerary is built around parks, shorter sight visits, and genuine downtime rather than a full museum-and-monument checklist.

Quick facts

Best for
Kids 4+; younger kids do fine with a slower pace
Getting around
Metro is efficient but has a lot of stairs — a lightweight stroller helps

Plan around their pace, not a museum checklist

Paris is one of the more forgiving European capitals for a family trip, as long as the itinerary is built around what actually holds a kid's attention rather than a standard adult sightseeing list. A shorter visit to a major sight, paired with genuine outdoor time, tends to beat a long museum day every time.

Sights that work well with kids

The Eiffel Tower, from the Champ de Mars

You don't need to go up to make this a highlight — the lawn at Champ de Mars gives a great view and space to run around, which often matters more to younger kids than the elevator ride.

Jardin du Luxembourg

Playgrounds, a pond where kids can rent small sailboats, and a carousel — one of the best all-around parks in the city for a family afternoon.

A Seine river cruise

An hour of sightseeing without any walking required, and a good option on a day when little legs are tired.

Cité des Sciences et de l'Industrie

A large, genuinely hands-on science museum with a dedicated area for younger children (Cité des Enfants) — one of the better rainy-day options in the city.

What to skip or shorten with young kids

  • The Louvre — go for a focused hour rather than attempting the whole museum; the Mona Lisa room alone involves significant crowds and waiting
  • Versailles as a full day trip works better for kids 8+ who can handle the walking; younger kids may do better with just the gardens
  • Long, formal restaurant dinners — look instead for casual bistros that don't expect a multi-course evening

Practical tips

  • Many Paris museums are free for kids under 18 (EU residents) or under 26 (some museums, all EU residents) — check specific policies, as non-EU visitor rules vary
  • The Metro has a lot of stairs and few elevators; a lightweight umbrella stroller is easier to manage than a full-size one
  • Bakeries (boulangeries) are an easy, affordable lunch option that even picky eaters usually tolerate well

Frequently asked questions

Is Paris a good destination for young kids?

Yes, if the itinerary is built around their pace — shorter museum visits, more park time, and realistic expectations rather than a full adult sightseeing schedule.

Do you need to go up the Eiffel Tower with kids?

Not necessarily — the view and photo opportunity from the Champ de Mars lawn is a highlight on its own, without the lines and cost of going up.

How many days do you need in Paris with kids?

Four to five days is comfortable for the highlights at a family pace, with room for at least one unplanned, lower-key day.
